evals.prompt: my jlc assembly order got rejected, they say my bom and pos files dont match, what does that mean
evals.expected_output: Agent explains the BOM/CPL/board designator-set pairing requirement: every designator in the CPL must appear in the BOM (or be DNP-flagged), footprints must match the board, DNP rows kept rather than deleted; guides reconciliation: generate BOM from schematic, CPL from board, diff designator sets, fix one source, re-export both; suggests bom_lint.py to validate.
assertions: response explains designator-set mismatch between BOM and centroid/CPL files
response prescribes reconciling from the two sources (schematic BOM, board positions)
response mentions DNP rows should be flagged not deleted
response recommends a lint/validation step before re-submitting

evals.prompt: is it fine to use 0402 10uf caps on my 3v3 rail, trying to keep the board small
evals.expected_output: Agent flags the DC-bias problem: class-2 ceramics lose effective capacitance under bias, a 0402 10uF at 3.3V might still be reasonable but at 12V would collapse (typical vendor curve example: 10u 0402 X5R at 12V ~ 3u effective); suggests checking the vendor DC-bias curve, size for effective capacitance, or stepping up to 0603/0805; notes quantity of decaps matters more than single-part headline value.
assertions: response explains DC-bias effective capacitance loss with a concrete example
response recommends checking vendor DC-bias curves or using larger case
response does not just assert yes or no without the mechanism

evals.prompt: checking my parts before i freeze the bom, half of these are marked NRND on mouser, does that matter for a hobby build
evals.expected_output: Agent explains lifecycle semantics (Active/NRND/EOL): for a one-off hobby build NRND matters little today but means the part (and the design) dies on the next reorder; for any production or repeated build it is a scheduled redesign; advises checking date of status, recording it in BOM notes, and finding active alternates for at least single-source NRND parts.
assertions: response explains NRND meaning and its different weight for hobby vs production
response advises recording status + date in the BOM
response suggests alternates for single-source or NRND parts

evals.prompt: got a bunch of values in my bom like 4k99 5k1 5k23 resistors all 0603, feels excessive
evals.expected_output: Agent confirms consolidation instinct: E24 for routine pullups/dividers (4.7k, 5.1k), E96 only where the circuit math genuinely needs precision; each distinct value is a separate reel/line/stock mistake; suggests value-merge pass and reports via bom_lint consolidation warning.
assertions: response validates consolidation with E24/E96 reasoning
response explains the inventory/assembly cost of distinct values
response mentions a concrete tool or pass to do the merge

evals.prompt: im writing a bill of materials for my new kitchen cabinets, help me cost the plywood
evals.expected_output: No PCB skill triggers — physical woodworking BOM, not electronic. Agent answers the woodworking question directly.
assertions: response does not apply PCB BOM skill guidance to cabinet making
response handles the request as woodworking/costing
